turns.prompt_text: https://whitepaper.actor/#background I'm reading this whitepaper. What is the web-actor programming model?
turns.response_html:
Based on the whitepaper, the web-actor programming model is a language-agnostic model for building serverless, cloud-based microapps, automation programs, and agents. Inspired by the UNIX philosophy applied to cloud computing, Actors are designed to make software tools easy to develop, share, run, integrate, and build upon.

Here are the core components and concepts of the web-actor programming model:

1. What is an Actor?

An Actor is essentially a program packaged inside a Docker container that:

  • Accepts a well-defined JSON input.
  • Performs an isolated task (ranging from filling out a form or sending an email to crawling an entire website or running an AI agent).
  • Persists its state and can run for anywhere from seconds to hours.
  • Optionally produces a well-defined JSON output.

2. Core Elements of an Actor

  • Dockerfile: Specifies the source code, how it is built, and how it is run.
  • Documentation (README.md): Explains what the Actor does.
  • Input & Output Schemas: Define the expected structure of JSON inputs and outputs. Platforms use these schemas to automatically generate user interfaces, API documentation, validation rules, and integration workflows.
  • Out-of-the-Box Storage: Specialized data stores provided automatically to each Actor run.
  • Metadata: Details such as the Actor's name, description, author, and version.

3. Key Concepts in the Model

  • Standardized Input: Inputs are passed as JSON objects (acting similarly to command-line arguments in UNIX). Input schemas let systems automatically generate user interfaces and validate incoming parameters.
  • Isolated Run Environment: Actors execute inside an isolated Docker container with access to local files and the network. They can log output, set status messages, launch local web servers, or run as standalone REST APIs.
  • Specialized Storage:
    • Key-Value Store: Used for saving files, PDFs, screenshots, or persisting state (e.g., as JSON files).
    • Dataset: An append-only table-like storage designed for structured series of data (such as web scraping or data processing results) that can be easily exported to JSON, CSV, Excel, etc.
  • Interoperability & Integrations: Actors are built to easily interact with one another (one Actor can call another, use webhooks, or chain outputs to inputs) and integrate smoothly into external workflows via REST APIs, SDKs (such as Node.js and Python), or automation tools like Make and Zapier.

What Actors Are Not

Actors are not designed for long-running dependable storage workloads (like SQL databases) because execution can migrate between servers, nor are they optimized for high-frequency, ultra-low-latency microsecond HTTP request-response APIs (though they can run web servers or "standby" modes for handling lightweight API calls).
